chunks: 500 - Sālim ibn Mukram narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

A pillow of earth should be made for him, and a clod should be placed behind his back so that he does not lie flat. All the knots of his shroud should be untied, his face uncovered, then supplication should be made for him, and it should be said: “O Allah, Your servant, the son of Your servant, and the son of Your maidservant has come down to You, and You are the best with whom one may lodge. O Allah, make his grave spacious for him, prompt him with his proof, join him to his Prophet, and protect him from the evil of Munkar and Nakīr.”

Then place your right hand beneath his right shoulder and your left hand upon his left shoulder, and shake him firmly, saying: “O so-and-so son of so-and-so, Allah is your Lord, Muḥammad is your Prophet, Islam is your religion, and ʿAlī is your Walī and your Imam.” Then name the Imams عليهم السلام one by one until the last of them: “Your Imams are guiding and righteous Imams.” Then repeat the talqīn to him another time.

And when you place the bricks upon him, then say: “O Allah, have mercy on his estrangement, join his loneliness, comfort his desolation, calm his fear, and settle upon him from Your mercy a mercy by which he has no need of the mercy of anyone besides You. And gather him with the one whom he used to follow in wilayah.” Whenever you visit his grave, supplicate for him with this supplication while facing the qiblah and with your hands upon the grave.
Then when you come out from the grave, say, while shaking the dust from your hands: “Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we return.”

Then cast dust upon him with the backs of your hands three times and say: “O Allah, in faith in You and affirmation of Your Book: this is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth.” For whoever does that and says these words, Allah writes for him a good deed for every particle.

Then when his grave has been leveled, pour water over his grave, placing the grave before you while you are facing the qiblah. Begin pouring the water at his head and move with it around his grave from its four sides until you return to the head without interrupting the water. If any water remains, pour it upon the middle of the grave. Then place your hand upon the grave, supplicate for the deceased, and seek forgiveness for him.”

key_terms.التَّلْقِينَ: prompting the deceased with the articles of faith and Imams
key_terms.اللَّبِنَ: the bricks or grave-lining pieces placed over the deceased
key_terms.حُجَّتَهُ: his proof or answer by which he is prompted in the grave
key_terms.مُنْكَرٍ: the grave-questioning angel mentioned in burial context
key_terms.نَكِيرٍ: the grave-questioning angel mentioned alongside Munkar
key_terms.وِسَادَةٌ: a pillow or support placed for the deceased from earth

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about talqīn, supplications, and recommended acts at the grave after burial?
ai.summary: This hadith describes recommended rites to be performed during burial and after interment, including talqīn, supplications, placing water on the grave, and seeking forgiveness for the deceased. It reflects both jurisprudential guidance for funeral practice and eschatological concern for the deceased in the grave and barzakh.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.500 - Salim ibn Mukram narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:

"A pillow of earth should be placed for the deceased, and a clump of soil behind their back to prevent them from lying flat. The knots of their shroud should be untied, their face uncovered, and supplications should be made:
Allāhumma ‘abduka wa ibnu ‘abdika wa ibnu amatika nazala bika wa anta khayru manzūlin bih.
Allāhumma ifsaḥ lahu fī qabrihi wa laqqinh ḥujjatahu wa alḥiqhu binabiyyihi wa qihi sharra Munkarin wa Nakīr
'O’ Allah (swt), this is Your servant, the child of Your servant and maidservant. They have returned to You, and You are the best to receive. O’ Allah (swt), expand their grave for them, teach them their proof, and join them with their Prophet. Protect them from the trial of Munkar and Nakir.'"

Then, place your right hand under their right shoulder and your left hand on their left shoulder, and shake them firmly while saying:
Yā Fulān ibn Fulān, Allāhu rabbuka, wa Muḥammadun nabiyyuka, wa al-Islāmu dīnuka, wa ‘Aliyyun walīyuka wa imāmuka
"O’ [name of the deceased], child of [father’s name], Allah (swt) is your Lord (azj), Muhammad is your Prophet, Islam is your religion, Ali is your guardian and Imam" - Name each of the Imams, ending with: 'Your Imams are the guides and the righteous.'
Then repeat the talqeen (prompting of faith) once more.

And when you put earth over him or when placing bricks over the grave, say:
Allāhumma irḥam ghurbatahu wa ṣil waḥdatahu wa ānis waḥshatahu wa āmin raw‘atahu wa askin ilayhi min raḥmatika raḥmatan yastaghnī bihā ‘an raḥmati man siwāk, wa uḥshuruhu ma‘a man kāna yatawallāh
"O’ Allah (swt), have mercy on their loneliness, connect their solitude, comfort their fear, and fill them with Your mercy so that they need no mercy from anyone other than You. Unite them with those they loved."
When visiting their grave, recite this supplication facing the Qibla, with hands on the grave.

Upon exiting the grave, while brushing the dirt off your hands, say:
Innā lillāhi wa innā ilayhi rāji‘ūn
"Indeed, we belong to Allah (swt), and indeed, to Him we shall return."

Throw dirt onto the grave with the backs of your hands three times, saying:
Allāhumma īmānan bika wa taṣdīqan bikitābika, hādhā mā wa‘adanā Allāhu wa rasūluhu wa ṣadaqa Allāhu wa rasūluhu
"O’ Allah (swt), we believe in You and affirm Your Book. This is what You and Your Messenger have promised, and Allah (swt) and His Messenger have spoken the truth."
Whoever performs this and says these words will earn a reward for every particle of soil.

Once the grave is made/leveled, pour water over it, beginning at the head and circling around all four sides, returning to the head without breaking the flow of water. If any water remains, pour it in the middle of the grave. Place your hand on the grave, supplicate for the deceased, and seek forgiveness for them.
